hook: Three customers report what they paid at a food truck for different orders. From those three receipts you can work out the price of each item. Finding several unknowns from several facts is solving a system, and it is how every model in this course gets its constants.

prereq.why: In $y = mx + b$, the slope is $m = -2$.
$1^2 + 4 = 5$, so the point is on the graph.

figure.caption: The system $y = 2x - 1$ and $y = -x + 5$ has one solution, $(2, 3)$, the point where the lines cross.

chain.cause: Write one equation for each fact (each data point)
chain.effect: a system with as many equations as unknowns

chain.cause: Substitute or add equations to remove one variable at a time
chain.effect: one equation in one variable, which you solve

chain.cause: Work back up and check every original equation
chain.effect: all the unknowns, at full precision

ideas: A solution of a system makes every equation true at once; for two lines it is where they cross.
To fit $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ to three points, substitute each point to get three equations in $a$, $b$ and $c$.
With a calculator, store each constant; rounding early spoils every value that comes after.

misconception.wrong: Substituting $(2, 11)$ into $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ gives $2a + 2b + c = 11$.
misconception.right: The input is squared for the $a$ term: $a(2)^2 + 2b + c = 11$, so $4a + 2b + c = 11$.

summary: Solve a system by substitution or elimination, removing one variable at a time. Fitting a model through data points means writing one equation per point and solving for the constants, stored at full precision.
